newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end lower on sales ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end lower on sales ahead of weekend.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed lower on Friday as participants were prompted to square their positions ahead of the long weekend amid uncertainty about domestic politics and worries over the New York stock market before a U.S. policy-making meeting, brokers said.
The key 225-issue Nikkei average closed down 210.61 points or 0.99 percent at 21,112.24. Its key December futures shed 140 points to 21,180.
"People wanted to unload their positions as much as possible ahead of the three-day weekend," said Kenichi Sagami, general manager at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
The market was aware of the possibility that Sumitomo's loss from the trading scandal would be higher than what had initially been announced, Nomura Securities said.
Shares in Miyakoshi Corp reached their maximum allowable single-day gain in the Friday afternoon session, gaining 100 yen to close at 600 yen.
It was the second largest percentage gainer in the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Traders said the share price was pushed up mainly by speculative investors' buying.
Shares in Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD) fell, pushed down by media reports that its earnings would be lower than expected.
The shares of the international telecommunications carrier fell 900 yen to close at 10,500 yen.
The second section index inched down 3.39 points to 2,103.22, with 15.10 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was also 2.40 points lower to close at 1,568.53.
